transcript:
[Doctor]: Hi, John. How are you doing today?

[Patient]: Hi, Doctor. I’m not doing too well. I’ve been having some severe abdominal pain.

[Doctor]: I'm sorry to hear that. Can you tell me more about the pain? How long has this been going on?

[Patient]: It’s been about three weeks now. The pain is constant and gets worse after I eat.

[Doctor]: Where exactly is the pain located?

[Patient]: It's primarily in the lower left part of my abdomen.

[Doctor]: Hmm, okay. Are there any other symptoms you’ve noticed?

[Patient]: Yes, I’ve lost my appetite, I’m constipated, and I’ve noticed some blood in my stool occasionally.

[Doctor]: That sounds quite concerning. Has the severity of your symptoms affected your daily life?

[Patient]: Yes, it has. I’ve had to stay home from work because of the pain.

[Doctor]: I see. Let’s go through a quick review of your systems. Apart from the abdominal pain, loss of appetite, constipation, and blood in your stool, have you noticed any other changes in your health?

[Patient]: Well, I’ve been in moderate distress because of the pain, and it’s really impacted my daily activities.

[Doctor]: Have you had any respiratory issues like shortness of breath or a cough?

[Patient]: No, nothing like that.

[Doctor]: How about any neurological issues, like numbness or tingling?

[Patient]: No, I haven't had any neurological issues.

[Doctor]: Any chronic pain elsewhere in your body?

[Patient]: Yes, I have chronic low back pain.

[Doctor]: Okay, let’s move on to the physical exam. I’ve reviewed your vital signs: your blood pressure is 138/85 mmHg, heart rate is 82 bpm, respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute, and your temperature is 98.6°F. Your oxygen saturation is 98% on room air. Everything seems within normal limits.

[Patient]: Alright.

[Doctor]: I’m going to examine your abdomen now. Please let me know if you feel any pain when I press down.

[Patient]: Alright.

[Doctor]: (pressing) How does this feel?

[Patient]: Ow, that’s really tender.

[Doctor]: I see. There is severe tenderness in the lower left quadrant. I also noticed a positive Murphy’s sign, but no rebound tenderness. Your bowel sounds are hypoactive.

[Patient]: What does that mean?

[Doctor]: It indicates that your intestines are not moving as they should be, which could be related to your constipation and abdominal pain. 

[Patient]: Okay.

[Doctor]: I also listened to your heart and lungs. Your heart sounds normal with no murmurs, and your lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Neurologically, you have no focal deficits.

[Patient]: That’s good to hear.

[Doctor]: Based on your symptoms and physical exam, I have a few concerns. We need to rule out any potential colorectal pathology, especially given your family history of colorectal cancer.

[Patient]: Oh, okay.

[Doctor]: I’m going to prescribe you Acetaminophen 500 mg to help manage the pain. You should take it every 6 hours as needed. Do you have any allergies to medications?

[Patient]: No, I don’t have any allergies.

[Doctor]: Great. I’ll prescribe 30 tablets for you. I also advise you to make some dietary modifications, specifically increasing your fiber intake and hydrating adequately. This should help with the constipation.

[Patient]: Alright, I can do that.

[Doctor]: I’ll refer you to Dr. Matthews, a gastroenterologist, for further evaluation. Given your family history and symptoms, it’s crucial that we investigate this thoroughly.

[Patient]: I understand.

[Doctor]: I’m also ordering a CT colonography to evaluate for any colorectal pathology, and an abdominal X-ray to rule out bowel obstruction. 

[Patient]: When will these tests be done?

[Doctor]: We’ll coordinate with the imaging center to schedule them as soon as possible. 

[Patient]: Okay.

[Doctor]: I’d like you to follow up with me in two weeks to review the results of the CT colonography and abdominal X-ray, and to assess how your symptoms are progressing.

[Patient]: Alright, I’ll do that.

[Doctor]: It’s important that you adhere to the prescribed medication and dietary changes. Also, I encourage you to quit smoking and reduce alcohol intake for your overall health improvement.

[Patient]: I’ll try my best.

[Doctor]: If your symptoms worsen or if you notice an increase in blood in your stool or experience severe abdominal pain, seek immediate medical attention.

[Patient]: Got it.

[Doctor]: Do you have any questions or concerns?

[Patient]: No, I think that covers everything.

[Doctor]: Alright, John. Thank you for coming in today. We’ll get these tests scheduled and see you back here in two weeks.

[Patient]: Thank you, Doctor.

[Doctor]: Take care and follow up with any changes or concerns you may have.

[Patient]: Will do. Thanks again.
